Neftegaz.ru (798203, 2023) then reports that in December 2021 Gazprom completed a CAPACITY-EXPANSION rebuild of that same Komsomolsk-Khabarovsk corridor -- 'построен участок... протяженностью 390,8 км (с учетом резервных ниток и подводных переходов)' (a 390.8 km section built, counting backup lines/underwater crossings), enabling capacity up to 20 bcm/y. So P2027 is best read as tracking THIS 2021 expansion/second-string build on the Komsomolsk-Khabarovsk corridor -- a genuine, later, physically-distinct construction project (its own length, its own completion date) layered on top of the original 472 km pipe that P0758's own recorded length already includes. CAVEAT flagged as a cross_row_lead for whoever researches P2027: the 472 km (original, per Gazprom) vs 390.8 km (as-built 2021 second string, per neftegaz.ru) figures need reconciling on P2027's own row -- these are two different numbers for related but not identical builds and P2027's LengthKnown should be checked against which one it actually represents before assuming either matches cleanly.

This 28.04 figure is plausibly a full future/ultimate design capacity (post further compressor buildout) rather than the capacity actually reached by the completed December-2021 expansion. Recommend keeping GEM's 20.00 bcm/y (it matches the most specific, dated, as-built claim) but this discrepancy deserves a second look by someone with time to pull the underlying 2014-corrected design documentation directly. SEGMENTCOST: the only value-supporting source found is en.rian.ru/sputnikglobe.com dated 2008-07-04 (Gazeta.ru/Nezavisimaya Gazeta/Vedomosti digest, headline 'Gazprom to spend $24 billion on Far Eastern gas pipeline') -- an exact match to GEM's recorded SegmentCost=24,000,000,000 USD, but this is a 2008 PRE-CONSTRUCTION cost ESTIMATE (upper end of a $21-24bn range reported that week), not a 2018 actual/final cost. GEM's SegmentCostYear=2018 therefore does not match any evidence found and is likely wrong (should probably read 2008, an estimate-year, and ideally ResearcherNotes should flag it as an estimate rather than an actual). Also note en.rian.ru and sputnikglobe.com are the SAME underlying wire story (RIA Novosti rebrand) -- one origin, not two independent sources, for this figure.
